meta.title: Pip v4 build guide
meta.note: Every line of step text traces to the doc named in its src list; fasteners are only listed where a doc states them.

steps.title: Wheel modules
body: Pip drives on four 6-inch omni wheels in a plus layout, one pointing forward.
Each module holds a wheel on a 40 mm shaft that runs in two bearings inside a two-plate pod, so wheel loads never reach the motor's bearing.
Each motor goes into its printed can, which points inward and drives the wheel hub.
fasteners: Motor into its can: 3 screws
Torque pin, then the hub adapter: 4 screws

subs.caption: Set out the four wheel modules in a plus shape, with one wheel pointing forward. Each wheel turns on a 40 mm shaft that runs in two bearings inside its two-plate pod.
Set a printed motor can on each module. The can points inward, toward the middle of the base, and drives the wheel hub.
Slide each motor into its can and fix it with 3 screws, then fit the torque pin and bolt on the hub adapter with 4 screws.
fasteners: Motor into its can: 3 screws
Hub adapter: 4 screws

steps.title: Belly, casters and deck
body: The belly pan closes the bottom in four quarters. The base electronics sit in a diagonal bay and the power board on the belly.
Four lockable ball casters go into their guides, and the two ballast cradles go in at the back.
The ribbed deck and the skirt are each printed in four quarters, so every piece fits a 256 mm printer bed.
src: docs/RND_LOG.md, build-out step 4 and loop notes on casters and ballast

subs.caption: Lay out the four belly pan quarters that close the bottom of the base.
Fit the base electronics in their diagonal bay and the power board on the belly.
Fit the four lockable ball casters, each in its own guide.
Set the two ballast cradles at the back of the base.
Lay the four ribbed deck quarters on top of the wheel pods and fit the rim around them. Each quarter fits a 256 mm printer bed.
Fit the four skirt quarters around the sides and the liners into the wheel wells.

steps.title: Battery, ballast and lidar
body: The 6S battery slides into the centre bay from the back, between the four motor cans.
Two removable steel ballast stacks are bolted up and dropped into their cradles.
The lidar sits on the front edge of the deck; the bumper light ring goes round the skirt.
steps.caution: 24 V lithium battery: use the specified BMS (30 A or more), fuse every branch, and charge on a non-flammable surface.
src: docs/RND_LOG.md, build-out step 4 and the ballast loop note

subs.caption: Slide the 6S battery into the centre bay from the back, between the four motor cans.
Bolt up the two removable steel ballast stacks and drop them into their cradles at the back.
Fit the lidar on the front edge of the deck and the bumper light ring around the skirt.

steps.title: Mast, lift drive and carriage
body: The mast coupling goes on the deck. The upper body plugs into it blind (3 power plugs and a 12-pin pogo block) and a cam lever locks it.
The lift motor cartridge slides into its bracket behind the mast and drives a belt pulley.
The mast is a 60 × 60 mm aluminium tube with a ratchet strip on its back face. The carriage rides it on 8 small bearings; its spring pawl drops into the ratchet whenever power is off.
The top bracket carries the belt idler and the carry handle.
fasteners: Lift cartridge: 4 ear screws, M4 × 12 with washers
steps.note: The four lift ear screws can't yet be reached with a straight driver on the assembled robot.

subs.caption: Fit the mast coupling on the deck. Its blind-mate plug carries power (3 XT60 connectors) and signals (a 12-pin pogo block) up to the torso.
Fit the lift drive bracket on the deck, behind the mast coupling.
Slide the lift motor cartridge into its bracket and fix it through its 4 ears.
fasteners: Ears: 4 × M4 × 12 with washers

subs.caption: Lower the mast into the coupling and lock it with the cam lever. The mast is a 60 × 60 mm aluminium tube with a ratchet strip on its back face, and the lift belt runs up beside it.
Slide the carriage down the mast. It runs on 8 small bearings, and its spring pawl drops into the ratchet whenever the power is off.
Fit the top bracket, with the belt idler and the carry handle, on top of the mast.

steps.title: Torso
body: The electronics tray (Raspberry Pi 5 and the DC-DC converter) and the AI bay sit inside the torso.
The two torso halves close around the carriage. Their side windows are where the shoulder modules go next.
The e-stop button sits on top and the chest light on the front.

subs.caption: Fit the electronics tray, with the Raspberry Pi 5 and the DC-DC converter, and the AI bay above it.
Close the two torso halves around the carriage. Their side windows are where the shoulders go.
Fit the e-stop button on top of the torso and the chest light on the front.

steps.title: Shoulder pitch modules
body: Each shoulder is a printed bracket with a one-piece pitch shaft and its big pulley. It goes into the torso's side window.
Fit the outer wall, then the pitch hub and the spring balancer (die spring, cord and pulley) that offsets the arm's weight.
The motor cartridge comes up through a slot in the bracket wall and slides into place along its axis; the belt goes on its small pulley and is tensioned with the idler.
fasteners: Outer wall: 3 × M4
Motor ears: 2 × M4 × 12 and 2 × M4 × 16 (from the pulley side), washers and nuts
Belt idler: M4 jack screw, then lock the M5 axle
Strap across the exit slot: 4 × M4
steps.note: Four of the pitch screws can't yet be reached with a straight driver on the assembled robot.

subs.caption: Slide each shoulder bracket into the side window of the torso.
Fit the one-piece pitch shaft, with its big pulley, into the bracket.
Close the bracket with its outer wall and 3 M4 screws.
fasteners: Outer wall: 3 × M4

subs.caption: Fit the pitch hub on the outer end of the shaft, and the spring balancer (a die spring, a cord and a pulley) that offsets the arm's weight.
Bring the motor cartridge up through the slot in the bracket wall.
Push the cartridge along its axis into its seat and bolt it through its 4 ears. Then put the belt on its small pulley and tension it with the idler.
fasteners: Ears: 2 × M4 × 12, and 2 × M4 × 16 from the pulley side, with washers and nuts
Idler: M4 jack screw, then lock the M5 axle
Strap across the exit slot: 4 × M4

steps.title: Shoulder roll
body: The roll link's ferrule slides onto the pitch hub. One V-band clamp holds the whole arm on, so an arm comes off in one move.
The roll motor fits inside the roll link, in line with the shoulder: a direct drive with no belt. A rear plate with crush sleeves and two steel stop bushes bolts it in.
The output adapter sits on 3 bonded dowels, and the clock spring carries the cables across the joint.
fasteners: Motor: 6 × M4 × 25 countersunk + 2 × M4 × 25 cap screws
Output adapter: 3 dowels with retaining compound
Arm clamp: 3-inch quick-release V-band
steps.note: Two of the eight motor screws are blocked for a straight driver.

subs.caption: Slide the roll link's ferrule onto the pitch hub. One V-band clamp holds the whole arm on, so an arm comes off in one move.
fasteners: Arm clamp: 3-inch quick-release V-band

subs.caption: Fit the roll motor inside the roll link, in line with the shoulder, so it drives the arm directly with no belt. Screw it in from the back through a rear plate with crush sleeves and two steel stop bushes.
fasteners: Motor: 6 × M4 × 25 countersunk and 2 × M4 × 25 cap screws

subs.caption: Fit the output adapter to the front of the motor on 3 dowels bonded with retaining compound.
fasteners: 3 dowels with retaining compound

subs.caption: Fit the roll clock spring, a wound ribbon cassette that carries the cables across the joint.

steps.title: Upper-arm yaw stage
body: The clevis and yaw block (one printed piece) bolt to the roll motor's output, and the clevis closes behind the motor.
The one-piece yaw shaft (40-tooth pulley and spring hub) goes up into the top plate; the bottom plate bolts on and the flange goes on last.
The yaw motor cartridge drops in along its axis. A steel pin stops the yaw at ±155°.
fasteners: Clevis: M5 screws in 8 crush sleeves
Motor ears: 4 × M4 × 12 with washers, side-fed nuts
Belt: 315 mm closed belt, 20 : 40 teeth
steps.note: Four of the yaw ear screws can only be reached with a ball-end driver at an angle so far.

subs.caption: Bolt the clevis and yaw block, which are one printed piece, to the roll motor's output, then close the clevis behind the motor. The clevis takes M5 screws in 8 crush sleeves.
fasteners: Clevis: M5 screws in 8 crush sleeves

subs.caption: Push the one-piece yaw shaft, with its 40-tooth pulley and spring hub, up into the top plate.
Bolt the bottom plate on underneath.
Fit the yaw flange last. A steel pin stops the yaw at plus or minus 155 degrees.
Drop the yaw motor cartridge in along its axis and fix it through its 4 ears with side-fed nuts. Its belt is a 315 mm closed loop from a 20-tooth to a 40-tooth pulley.
fasteners: Ears: 4 × M4 × 12 with washers and side-fed nuts

steps.title: Upper arm and elbow
body: Bond the carbon-fibre tube into the upper bone with structural epoxy and let it cure overnight.
The upper bone rises onto the yaw flange and is tied with 6 screws in crush sleeves from the top of the tube.
The elbow belt cassette goes in from below, with its one-piece shaft and the aluminium core tube bonded inside. Seat caps hold the bearings.
fasteners: Yaw flange tie: 6 × M3 × 45 in crush sleeves
Seat caps: 2 × M4 and 2 × M3
Structural epoxy

subs.caption: Bond the carbon-fibre tube into the upper bone with structural epoxy and let it cure overnight. Then raise the upper bone onto the yaw flange and tie it with 6 screws in crush sleeves from the top of the tube.
fasteners: Yaw flange tie: 6 × M3 × 45 in crush sleeves
Structural epoxy

subs.caption: Push the elbow belt cassette in from below. Its one-piece shaft has an aluminium core tube bonded inside.
Screw on the seat caps that hold the elbow shaft's bearings.
fasteners: Seat caps: 2 × M4 and 2 × M3

subs.caption: Close the bottom of the upper arm with the bone cap, and fit the elbow's joint encoder on the inner side.

steps.title: Elbow motor cartridge
body: Fit the motor into its printed can from the rear, then close it with the rear cap.
Fit the steel drive stub to the motor output, then add the key, the 20-tooth pulley and the end bearing.
The cartridge slides straight in along its axis, stub first, and bolts on through its 4 ears. To swap a motor later, undo those 4 screws; the belt stays on, and the swap takes about 3 minutes.
fasteners: Rear cap: 3 × M3 × 8 into the motor, 2 × M3 × 10 into the can's inserts
Drive stub: 8 × M3 × 6 with threadlocker
Ears: 4 × M4 × 12 with washers into captive nuts
src: docs/rnd/assembly_seq.md (elbow swap: straight out along its axis)
steps.note: These four ear screws can't yet be reached with a straight driver on the assembled arm.

subs.caption: Slide the motor into its printed can from the rear.
Close the can with the rear cap, using 3 M3 × 8 screws into the motor and 2 M3 × 10 screws into the can's inserts.
fasteners: Rear cap: 3 × M3 × 8 into the motor and 2 × M3 × 10 into the can's inserts

subs.caption: Bolt the steel drive stub to the motor output with 8 M3 × 6 screws and threadlocker.
fasteners: Drive stub: 8 × M3 × 6 with threadlocker

subs.caption: Fit the key and the 20-tooth pulley on the stub, then press the end bearing on.
Slide the cartridge straight in along its axis, stub first, and bolt it through its 4 ears into captive nuts. To swap the motor later you undo only these 4 screws, and the belt stays on.
fasteners: Ears: 4 × M4 × 12 with washers into captive nuts

steps.title: Forearm, wrist and hand
body: The forearm (a carbon tube bonded between two printed ends) clamps onto the elbow shaft.
The wrist motor goes into its can, with bolted can and output flanges, and slides into the forearm end.
The hand goes on the wrist: palm, wrist-roll spindle and end cap, then the gripper with its servo, fin-ray finger, palm distance sensor and wrist camera.
fasteners: Forearm clamp: 2 × M5
Wrist can flange and output flange: 6 × M3 each, into inserts
Palm: 6 × M3
src: docs/rnd/assembly_seq.md (wrist and palm screws, wrist-roll spindle)

subs.caption: Bond the carbon tube into the two printed forearm ends, then clamp the forearm onto the elbow shaft with 2 M5 screws.
fasteners: Forearm clamp: 2 × M5

subs.caption: Fit the wrist motor into its can with its bolted can and output flanges, and slide it into the end of the forearm.
fasteners: Can flange and output flange: 6 × M3 each, into inserts

subs.caption: Fit the hand to the wrist: the palm with 6 M3 screws, then the wrist-roll spindle, its bearings and the end cap.
fasteners: Palm: 6 × M3

subs.caption: Fit the gripper with its servo and fin-ray finger, the palm distance sensor and the wrist camera.

steps.title: Head
body: The pan motor sleeve sits on the top bracket, and the yoke goes on it.
The tilt motor sleeve goes on one side of the yoke and a bearing on the other.
The head shell goes on the yoke, then the 7-inch touch screen face, the dark visor, the eye lights and the depth camera.

subs.caption: Fit the pan motor sleeve on the top bracket.
Fit the yoke on the pan motor.
Fit the tilt motor sleeve on one side of the yoke and the bearing on the other.
Lower the head shell onto the yoke.
Fit the 7-inch touch screen face, the dark visor, the eye lights and the depth camera.

steps.title: Covers
body: The covers close the robot in: every belt, pulley, coupling and motor can is enclosed, with openings of 8 mm or less so fingers can't reach them.
On each arm: the yaw hood and band, the elbow bay, the elbow cap and door, and the forearm and wrist covers.
On the body: the lift drive cover, the belt duct up the mast, the spine pod, the torso collars and the mast cap.

subs.caption: Cover the lift drive and fit the belt duct up the back of the mast.
Fit the spine pod and the two torso collars. They ride up and down with the torso.
Fit the mast cap over the top bracket.
On each arm, fit the yaw hood over the yaw stage and the band around it.
Close each elbow with the elbow bay cover, the elbow cap and its door.
Fit the forearm and wrist covers from both sides. With every cover on, the belts, pulleys and motors are fully enclosed, and no opening is wider than 8 mm.

steps.title: Finished robot
body: The finished robot has two arms with six joints and a gripper each, a head on a lifting torso and a four-wheel omni base, driven by 21 actuators in all.
Estimated first build: about 24 hours of hands-on work plus about 354 hours of unattended printing (14.8 kg of PETG and ASA). One arm, the first milestone, is about 6 hours hands-on.
Next come wiring, sensors and bring-up. Test the lift pawl, the e-stop and the watchdog before any powered arm motion.

subs.caption: This is the finished robot as the design files describe it. Turn it around to look at it from every side.
